text: Soapy walked east to a quiet street. <break time="0.8s" /> Where an old church stood. <break time="0.8s" /> With soft light shining. <break time="0.8s" /> Through a violet window. <break time="0.8s" /> Inside the organist was practicing an anthem for Sunday. <break time="0.8s" /> And the sweet music drifted out. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the night. <break time="0.8s" /> Soapy had known that anthem well. <break time="0.8s" /> In the days. <break time="0.8s" /> When his life held a mother, roses, friends, and dreams. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly a wonderful change. <break time="0.8s" /> Came over his soul. <break time="0.8s" /> And he saw with horror. <break time="0.8s" /> The pit of wasted days and dead hopes. <break time="0.8s" /> Feeling a new strength in his heart. <break time="0.8s" /> Soapy decided to pull himself out of the pit. <break time="0.8s" /> And become a real man again. <break time="0.8s" /> A fur dealer had once offered him. <break time="0.8s" /> A job as a driver. <break time="0.8s" /> And tomorrow he would go. <break time="0.8s" /> And ask for it. <break time="0.8s" /> If I had a job. <break time="0.8s" /> I would be somebody in the world. <break time="0.8s" /> He thought. <break time="0.8s" /> And his heart filled with hope. <break time="0.8s" /> Just then Soapy felt a hand on his arm. <break time="0.8s" /> And he turned. <break time="0.8s" /> To see the broad face of a policeman. <break time="0.8s" /> What are you doing here. <break time="0.8s" /> Asked the policeman. <break time="0.8s" /> And when Soapy answered Nothing. <break time="0.8s" /> He said, Then come along. <break time="0.8s" /> Three months on the Island. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the judge in the Police Court. <break time="0.8s" /> The next morning.
